description: Declarative intended EXECUTE-grant matrix for every final SECURITY DEFINER function in schema public, after all canonical migrations. This file is the authority: scripts/check-security-definer-hardening.mjs reconstructs the effective ACL from the migration chain and fails if it disagrees with this matrix, and the fresh-DB certification compares live pg_proc ACLs against it. Adding a SECURITY DEFINER function without adding it here fails the gate.
principals: PUBLIC, anon, authenticated and service_role are four DISTINCT privilege principals. On Supabase, ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES grants EXECUTE on every new public-schema function to anon, authenticated and service_role as explicit per-role ACL entries, separate from the PUBLIC pseudo-role entry. REVOKE EXECUTE ... FROM PUBLIC therefore does NOT revoke anon or authenticated.

intended_caller_semantics.authenticated_rls_helper: Referenced by RLS policy expressions. Policy expressions evaluate with the CALLER's privileges, so authenticated EXECUTE is load-bearing: revoking it breaks tenant isolation.
intended_caller_semantics.authenticated_rpc: Invoked from application code through createSupabaseServerClient (anon key + session cookie, resolving to the authenticated role). Each re-derives authority server-side from auth.uid(); caller-supplied workspace/project/actor parameters are never trusted.
intended_caller_semantics.service_role: Invoked only through createSupabaseServiceRoleClient, or (purge_expired_nonces) reserved for a future scheduled job. No client role may execute.
intended_caller_semantics.internal_security_definer_only: Primary legitimate invocation path is from OTHER SECURITY DEFINER functions, which execute as the function owner and therefore do not require a client-role grant. Direct client EXECUTE is denied. service_role EXECUTE remains explicitly granted for operational and administrative access, not because a service_role caller is the routine path.
intended_caller_semantics.trigger_only: RETURNS TRIGGER. Not invocable as an RPC: PostgreSQL refuses direct calls to trigger functions regardless of EXECUTE, and PostgREST excludes trigger-returning functions from the /rpc/ surface. Grants here are privilege hygiene, not an exploitable boundary.

functions.rationale: INTERNAL SECURITY-DEFINER-CALL-ONLY. Its primary legitimate invocation path is from other SECURITY DEFINER functions (record_operational_decision), which execute as the function owner and therefore do not need a client-role grant. 20260611000000 revoked PUBLIC and deliberately issued no grant. Direct client EXECUTE denied; service_role EXECUTE retained for operational/administrative access.

functions.name: operational_workspace_role
functions.rationale: INTERNAL SECURITY-DEFINER-CALL-ONLY. Primary legitimate invocation path is from other SECURITY DEFINER functions (can_write_operational_project, persist_governed_material_action, revoke_governed_material_action), which execute as the function owner. Zero RLS-policy references. 20260611000000 revoked PUBLIC and deliberately issued no grant. Direct client EXECUTE denied; service_role EXECUTE retained.

functions.name: p2_08_validate_execution_governance
functions.rationale: INTERNAL SECURITY-DEFINER-CALL-ONLY. 20260905000000 states verbatim: 'intentionally no authenticated grant: only the bounded SECURITY DEFINER RPCs call it.' Primary legitimate invocation path is from dispatch_internal_task_execution and transition_internal_task_execution. Direct client EXECUTE denied; service_role EXECUTE retained.

functions.name: persist_governed_material_action
functions.rationale: Authenticated governed-action RPC (operational-flow-service.ts:318). Already correct on hosted: 20260903000000 revoked PUBLIC and anon explicitly. Rejects anonymous callers with material_action_unauthenticated.

functions.name: prepare_decision_evidence_link
functions.rationale: TRIGGER-ONLY. RETURNS TRIGGER, bound to trg_prepare_decision_evidence_link (BEFORE INSERT on public.decision_evidence_links). PostgreSQL refuses direct invocation of a trigger function regardless of EXECUTE ('trigger functions can only be called as triggers'), and PostgREST excludes trigger-returning functions from the /rpc/ surface entirely, so the historical PUBLIC grant was never a callable privilege boundary. Revoked here as privilege hygiene, NOT as remediation of an exploitable RPC. Trigger execution is unaffected: triggers run as the table owner and do not consult the client role's EXECUTE privilege.

functions.name: purge_expired_nonces
functions.rationale: SERVICE_ROLE / FUTURE CRON ONLY. Deletes expired rows from public.agent_attestation_nonces. Has no internal authorization check of any kind and zero call sites in src/. Because it is SECURITY DEFINER it executes as the owner and therefore bypassed the table-level revoke that 20260826000000 applied to agent_attestation_nonces; the anon grant made that bypass reachable with only the publishable anon key. Direct client EXECUTE denied.
